attachments.origin_landmark: obturator membrane and its bony margin (internal surface)
attachments.insertion_landmark: greater trochanter (medial surface, via lesser sciatic notch)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Makes a sharp ~90-degree turn around the lesser sciatic notch (acting as a pulley) between its origin and insertion -- a genuine anatomical redirection, not just a curved path.
functional_compartments.source: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_from: medial edge of the obturator foramen
motor_endplate_zones.method: modified Sihler's whole-mount nerve staining, 16 cadaveric specimens
motor_endplate_zones.notes: The intrapelvic portion of the muscle carries the neural arborization; the source states most of the extrapelvic portion (beyond the lesser sciatic notch) is tendinous and should be considered unsuitable as an injection site.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Yi KH, An MH, Lee JH, Lee HJ (2023) Surg Radiol Anat 45(10):1239-1244, doi:10.1007/s00276-023-03216-6 -- retrieved via PubMed

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082 -- lower-extremity muscle architecture (fascicle length, PCSA, sarcomere length) cadaver dataset

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Patient prone; transducer placed transversely over the posterior hip near the ischial spine/lesser sciatic notch, deep to gluteus maximus, to bring obturator internus into short axis for a direct intramuscular approach.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deep to gluteus maximus, superficial to the ischium and hip joint capsule.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Validated in a cadaveric model (5 pelvis specimens, 22-gauge 3.5-in needle): direct sonographic guidance for an intramuscular obturator internus injection placed 100% of the injectate within the muscle with no injury to the sciatic nerve or gluteal arteries in any specimen. For the chronic-pelvic-pain indication (rather than hip external-rotator spasticity), obturator internus is instead often approached transvaginally with EMG/nerve-stimulation guidance or under fluoroscopy/CT, targeting the intrapelvic portion described in motor_endplate_zones since the extrapelvic portion is largely tendinous.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Smith J, Wisniewski SJ, Wempe MK, Landry BW, Sellon JL (2012) J Ultrasound Med 31(10):1597-1608, doi:10.7863/jum.2012.31.10.1597 -- retrieved via PubMed
